title: fix(types,components): calendar date-value keys cross the JSON/TS boundary once (objectui#10293)
body:
Clause-②: yes

Closes #10293
Part of #7759 (group D, ruling D1-(iii): comments 5617221514, 5617465269 and 5617614225)

## What changed

| face | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `form.ts` `CalendarSchema.defaultValue` / `.value` (TS declaration) | `Date \| Date[]` | `Date \| string` |
| `form.zod.ts` `CalendarSchema.defaultValue` / `.value` (mirror) | `z.union([z.string(), z.date()])` | unchanged. Only the `.describe()` text now names the ISO 8601 authoring type |
| `ui:calendar` renderer (`packages/components/src/renderers/form/calendar.tsx`) | forwards `schema.value \|\| schema.defaultValue` to `DayPicker` untouched | coerces a string through `toDisplayDate` (`@object-ui/core`, the objectui#10183 helper). A `Date` or nothing passes through unchanged |
| parity ledger (`zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`) | rows in `KnownDrift`, `WiderThanDeclared` and `WIDER_ARMS` | all three removed. Header figures re-derived by the file's own pins: KnownDrift 46/85 to 45/83, and Wider 19/29/36 to 18/27/32 (CONCRETE 24 to 22, unions 7 to 5), with history sentences |

The docs page (`content/docs/components/form/calendar.mdx`) documents the ISO string.

## Per-key judgement (ruling 5617465269 asks for it)

- **Does spec declare it?** No. `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 has no `ui:calendar` primitive. Its `calendar` hits are all the list-view type. So this is an objectui-owned key, and the read site governs.
- **Does the `z.date()` arm stay?** Yes, following in-tree precedent. Every settled date-value key in `form.zod.ts` keeps it: `DatePickerSchema.defaultValue` / `.value` (TS `Date | string`, mirror `string | Date`) and this schema's own `minDate` / `maxDate`. JSON can never carry a `Date`. In-process callers that `safeParse` a `Date` keep working.
- **The string arm stays `z.string()`.** No ISO-format refinement was added. No sibling date key has one, and it would narrow the mirror beyond what the ledger measured. This is listed as an open question in the report.

## The read site, measured before editing (base `5ea623eab`)

This used a probe render of `ui:calendar` on a frozen clock `2026-09-03T10:35Z`, in forked vitest children:

| value | UTC | America/Los_Angeles |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `new Date(2026, 8, 15)` | selects 15th | selects 15th |
| `"2026-09-15"` (value or defaultValue) | selects 15th | **selects 14th** |
| `"2026-09-15T12:00:00Z"` | selects 15th | selects 15th |
| `"not a date"` | selects nothing | selects nothing |

So a string already reached `DayPicker`: date-fns parses it with the engine's own `Date` parse. What was missing was the date-only convention. A date-only string is UTC midnight, read back in local time. After the change, the date-only row selects the 15th in both zones. Every other row is unchanged.

## Pins, and proof that they redden on revert

- `packages/types/src/__tests__/calendar-date-value-boundary-10293.test.ts`: type-level equality of both faces with `Date | string | undefined`, plus a `@ts-expect-error` on `Date[]`. At runtime it checks that the mirror accepts date-only, date-time and `Date` values and refuses a list.
- `packages/components/src/renderers/form/__tests__/calendar.dateValueZone-10293.test.tsx`: an ISO string selects the same day as the equivalent `Date`. The file has UTC cases, driven west cases (LA, with a rig case and a fixture-validity case) and driven east control cases (Shanghai). It is registered as a fifth pin in `scripts/__tests__/date-only-zone-pins-10183.test.ts`, the forks-pool driver that PR #10266 built.
- **Renderer ablation** (committed first, then `ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, anchor `selected={toSelected(...)}` replaced by the raw read). The anchor went from 1 hit to 0, and the blob went from `6e729e18d454` to `3323137ca363`. The driver went red: `Tests 2 failed | 4 passed (6)`. The calendar pin failed on exactly one case, the west date-only case. Restore: the blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **Declaration ablation** (`value?: Date | string` back to `Date | Date[]`). `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exited 2 with 7 errors: 4 in the new pin and 3 in `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`, where `form.zod.ts#CalendarSchema` became "not assignable to type 'never'" in the ledger assertions. Restore: the blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Local gates, at `248f23de5`

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check`: VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `vitest run packages/types/` plus the calendar pin plus the zone driver: `Test Files 217 passed (217)`, `Tests 4939 passed | 7 skipped`. The 7 skipped are the driven zone cases in the normal run. The driver itself passed, so they ran in the forked child.
- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/components^...' build` (8 of 47 projects): exit 0. Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components type-check`, and `vitest run packages/components/src/renderers/form/`: `62 passed`, `427 passed | 7 skipped`.
- `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on the 7 changed lintable files: 7 files, 0 errors, 15 warnings. All 15 are existing `no-explicit-any` hits (`calendar.tsx` had 3 on `origin/main` and still has 3). Type-aware linting is not configured (`eslint.config.js` has no `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot change the verdict for any untouched file.
- `check-changeset-presence`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:doc-types`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-example-ids`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:component-surface-parity`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check-changeset-no-major`: all exit 0.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:doc-snippets` and `check:doc-examples`, which exit 2 with PRECONDITION NOT MET. They need a build of 34 packages. They are left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- ⚠️ **The declaration gives up `Date[]`.** The issue said the declaration was `Date`. On `main` it was `Date | Date[]`. The ruling text and the dispatch both name `string | Date`, so `Date[]` left. The effect is TypeScript-only. The mirror never accepted a list, no in-tree caller passes one, and the renderer still forwards an array unchanged, so `multiple` mode with an in-process `Date[]` still renders. The changeset states this. If the list arm should stay, the fix is to keep `Date[]` in the declaration and keep a `KnownDrift` row for it. The report carries this as an open question.
- The calendar does not navigate to a selected date outside the current month: there is no `defaultMonth`. That was true before this change and is unchanged, so the pins freeze the clock inside the month under test.
- Two findings on the same node are outside this card. They are reported to the seat for filing, not fixed here: a scalar `value` under `mode: 'multiple'` throws at render, and every value the mirror accepts under `mode: 'range'` selects nothing.
- Commit `248f23de5` carries a harness-shaped `Co-Authored-By` trailer that names the model. The os-dev contract asks for model-free trailer pairs. History is not rewritten; this is reported only.
